elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 reads: "This Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York." The Singapore choice-of-law words are gone and New York is within the accepted set (deterministic check "governing law within the accepted set" ok).

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Retained 28.2: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction... Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court..." The carve-out is limited to temporary injunctive relief, which under the rule boundaries preserves the exclusive merits forum; the competing Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction words in 28.1 have been deleted, so no contradictory retained forum remains.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered 28.1 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is the preferred position rather than the fallback, so the fallback checklist is simply not the level pursued.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County; no Delaware, California, or London forum is designated. Again a consequence of pursuing the preferred level.

reasons: Preferred level is position-complete: 28.1 now selects New York law (element 1) and the pre-existing 28.2 already gives the state and federal courts in New York County exclusive jurisdiction with only a customary temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out elsewhere (element 2). No element is merely promised in the comment.
Fallback level is not met (New York law and New York courts rather than Delaware/California/England and Wales), which is expected and harmless because a single complete level suffices.

Minimal: the edit touches only the jurisdiction words and the forum words in 28.1, as the redline guidance directs. Deleting the Singapore exclusive-jurisdiction phrase is necessary, not cosmetic, because it would otherwise directly contradict 28.2's exclusive New York County forum and leave an internally inconsistent clause. 28.2 is left entirely untouched, so the favourable existing exclusive-forum, personal-jurisdiction submission, venue waiver, and injunctive-relief language survives, and no operative term is duplicated (governing law sits only in 28.1, forum only in 28.2).

Preserves intent: the word "exclusively" and the sentence structure of 28.1 are retained, no defined term is orphaned (Confidential Information remains defined at 16.1 and the 28.2 carve-out reference to confidential information and intellectual property is undisturbed), and no cross-reference is dangling. Unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, and commercial mechanics are unaffected.

Margin comment is compliant in tone and content: it states what changed and why in two sentences, cites the accepted position, and offers the Delaware/California/England and Wales fallback without lecturing.

Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original 28.1 Singapore law plus exclusive Singapore venue is Vendor-side foreign law and venue outside the accepted list, i.e. walk-away territory, so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale note.
